method: Fresh independent review of every one of the 112 assigned current files. Read AGENTS.md first; inspected the complete deployment implementation, fixed launchers and privilege boundaries, release/update/rollback/recovery transitions, ownership and stop proofs, provider/configuration composition, workspace/Git/recovery helpers, exact deployment and tooling test sources, CI, root configuration and documentation. Reviewed all assigned feature-evidence records as bounded historical feature claims, not prior audit conclusions or present-run proof. For the large capability inventory, inspected every method mapping, all unique assessments, all 50 evidence groups and all 15 additional workflows through structured projections, then checked all 178 identities against 175 generated JSON variants and verified 518 current source reference hashes. Reviewed the entire dependency lock metadata/graph and validated all 336 integrity entries plus the production dependency_input allowlist. Traced control-update persistent barriers, executor spool replay/admission, provider layer host-policy preservation, initial-install retries and native helper retention boundaries against their fault-injection tests. Ran only the explicitly listed targeted local checks. No previous implementation or history, prior audit reports/conclusions, personal configuration, remote host mutation, paid inference or external MCP was consulted or executed. Source remained frozen throughout.

checks.details: Production dependency_input accepted package, workspace policy and lock; every resolution entry was the expected registry-only SHA-512 form and decoded to exactly 64 bytes. No dependency installation or network fetch.
Checked distinct method identities, generated JSON coverage, declared classification/status totals and group membership. Referenced prior audit/work evidence was not opened.

checks.command: HARNESS_TEST_PYTHON=<bundled Python 3.12.14> node scripts/run-tests.mjs --targeted <six exact listed files>
checks.initialAttempt: The first invocation set PYTHON instead of HARNESS_TEST_PYTHON and was blocked by the WindowsApps placeholder (python-interpreter-unavailable); no tests ran. Retried with the documented explicit interpreter and all 29 passed.

checks.details: The fixture-internal empty/skipped Python cases are expected negative assertions; all 44 selected tooling tests passed. Git history fixtures were newly created isolated test repositories; previous application history was never read.

limitations: This is a complete source audit for the assigned deployment-release scope, not a full-suite run or production deployment acceptance.

Linux root ownership, real systemd/cgroups, network namespaces, subreaper cleanup, native-UID filesystem/Git execution and host reboot recovery were reviewed through code and test sources; these Linux-only integrations were not rerun on this Windows host.
No SSH operations, isolated host 120 changes, host 110 access, real provider credentials, external account/OAuth/email/Cloud/voice/AWS/MCP business calls or personal HOME/CODEX_HOME access occurred.
Historical feature evidence is explicitly point-in-time and often predates this freeze. Its limits were retained; source-pointer consistency does not independently reproduce external behavior.
No registry vulnerability/advisory lookup or third-party package-code audit was performed; the lock review covers pinned dependency graph, controlled overrides, integrity and build admission.
